subject: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 9:18 AM
Subject: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Hey Lauren,

We’re prepping for NovaCare’s security + architecture review this Thursday (they’re EU-based and want EU-only processing as a hard requirement). We’re positioning Dedicated in EU as the default, with residency pinning as the enforcement story.

Can you sanity-check / fill in the gaps for what we can confidently say?

1) Dedicated in EU:
- What’s our current set of supported EU regions we can sell against? (They asked specifically “EU West / Ireland” but are flexible if we’re clear.)
- Any constraints/notes re: capacity planning / lead time for reserved capacity?

2) Data residency pinning (Hosted + Dedicated):
- What’s the right phrasing for “no cross-region failover”? Do we have a supported override mechanism?
- If a client misconfigures the endpoint/region (e.g. US base URL), what happens? (HTTP code + error code?)
- Do we emit audit logs for allow/deny decisions? Any sample fields we should highlight (tenant id, decision, region, reason)?

3) MAP items:
- Need a clean set of next steps / owners for the POC. I started a MAP draft (attached) but want your input on product commitments vs. what’s still beta.

If you can, please send me 6–10 bullets we can use on the call + anything we should avoid promising.

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: NovaCare_MAP_v0.2.docx



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Markus — yep, this is the right framing. Here are the bullets + suggested language.

EU Dedicated (what we can commit to):
- We can deploy Dedicated capacity in EU (primary: eu-west). For NovaCare’s “EU West / Ireland” ask: we align to eu-west as the pinned region for their org/project.
- Dedicated gives isolation at the GPU pool + data plane level; routing stays within the dedicated pool/region per policy.
- Capacity: reserved capacity lead time depends on GPU class and commit size; for this deal we should assume we need an explicit capacity reservation in eu-west as part of the MAP. (Don’t imply “instant capacity.”)

Residency pinning behavior (customer-facing):
- When region pinning is enabled, routing is deterministic: requests are admitted only if the request’s effective region matches the pinned/allowed region policy.
- Cross-region fallback is disabled by default when pinned (i.e., we will return an error rather than failover to another region).
- Misconfiguration case (client hits the wrong regional endpoint): request is rejected before model execution with a machine-readable error code. Current contract:
  - HTTP 403
  - error_code: RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH
  - message includes: pinned_region, request_region, and “use the EU base URL / update SDK region config” guidance.
- Audit logs: yes, we emit audit events for policy evaluation and violations (allow/deny). We can share sample payloads but on the call I’d highlight: org_id/project_id, pinned_region/allowed_regions, request_region, decision (allow/deny), decision_reason.

What to avoid promising:
- Don’t say “automatic failover to another region” if they’re pinned EU-only.
- Don’t over-commit on retroactive migration of historical artifacts (out of scope for this phase).

I’m attaching the one-pager we’ve been using internally with the positioning + the short “what happens on mismatch” section.

If they ask about “override in emergencies,” I’d like Naomi/Aisha to weigh in on exactly how we talk about exceptions (I know there’s a GRC-backed process, but I don’t want us freelancing language).

-Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product Management, Redwood Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_EU_Residency_Pinning_OnePager_v3.pdf



From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 8, 2024 at 8:11 AM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Super helpful, thanks.

Re: override/emergency: NovaCare’s security lead (Amelia) explicitly asked last week: “If EU capacity is exhausted, can you fail over to US as last resort if we sign off?”

I told them “default is strict EU-only; exceptions are controlled and audited” but they’re going to press on the mechanics.

Naomi / Aisha — can you confirm:
- Do we have a formal exception workflow we can describe at a high level (approvals, time-bound, audit trail)?
- Do we have a term for it (e.g., ‘temporary cross-region allowance’) and can we say it’s opt-in only?

Also, Lukas — if you have a recommended way to talk about eu-west capacity + what we do instead of failover (queueing/429/explicit errors), send a note.

-Markus



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 8, 2024 at 9:26 AM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Confirming the intended story for exceptions (high level; keep it compliance-oriented):

- Default behavior with pinned_region is strict: no cross-region fallback; we return an explicit residency violation error before execution.
- We do support a controlled, opt-in exception mechanism for temporary cross-region allowance. Internally, it’s implemented as an override that permits cross-region fallback *only when explicitly enabled* for the tenant and only for approved regions.
- Exception workflow:
  1) Customer requests exception (scope: which regions; why; duration)
  2) Security Engineering + GRC approval required (documented)
  3) Exception is time-bound with an expiry date/time and is revocable
  4) Residency audit events reflect that the decision used an exception (so it shows up in SIEM export)

What I’d say on the call:
“Strict by default; exceptions are possible but require prior written approval, are time-bound, and are fully auditable.”

Lauren — your bullets are good; I’d add: “If capacity is constrained in-region, behavior is explicit (errors) rather than silent re-routing.”

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 8, 2024 at 10:07 AM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Adding the approved customer-facing phrasing from Security.

Recommended language (safe + accurate):
- “When EU region pinning is enabled, Redwood enforces residency at request admission and for downstream write paths in the Hosted/Dedicated service. Requests that would execute outside the pinned region are rejected before processing with a clear error code, and an audit event is emitted.”
- “Cross-region fallback is disabled by default for pinned tenants. Any temporary cross-region allowance is opt-in, time-bound, requires written approval, and is fully logged for compliance evidence.”

Avoid:
- “Data will never leave the EU under any circumstances.” (We can say “enforced by policy; exceptions require explicit approval,” which is what auditors expect anyway.)
- “We automatically fail over to another region” for EU-only customers.

If NovaCare wants sample audit payloads, we can provide in a follow-up email (better than screen-sharing raw JSON in the live call).

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO (Security Executive Sponsor)
Redwood Inference



From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 10, 2024 at 3:41 PM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

On the EU Dedicated capacity point:

- For the MAP, we should include a concrete “capacity reservation request” step with target GPU type + throughput target, so we can lock eu-west inventory.
- In-region capacity constraints: the preferred behavior is explicit backpressure (429/over-capacity) or an explicit “cannot satisfy request in-region” style error, rather than implicit cross-region rerouting.

Markus — if you want, I can join the last 10 minutes of the security review to answer region/capacity questions.

-Lukas



From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 10, 2024 at 4:34 PM
Subject: Re: NovaCare | EU Dedicated + data residency pinning - positioning & MAP inputs

Perfect — I’m updating the MAP now with:

MAP updates (draft):
- Redwood (Owner: Lukas): confirm eu-west capacity plan + reservation timeline for Dedicated
- Redwood (Owner: Lauren): confirm Dedicated SKU + residency pinning enablement requirements + any beta flags
- Redwood (Owner: Naomi): provide exception workflow one-pager (high level) + what gets logged
- Redwood (Owner: Markus): send NovaCare a follow-up with (a) approved language, (b) sample audit event payloads, (c) endpoint/SDK region configuration guidance
- NovaCare: provide required pinned region list + confirmation whether exceptions are acceptable and under what approval path

Lauren — can you join the call for 15 min at the beginning? They’ll ask “what exactly is Dedicated in EU vs Hosted in EU” and I want you to anchor that.

Invite is on your calendar already (Thu 11:00am PT / 8:00pm CET). If timing doesn’t work, I’ll use your bullets verbatim.

Thanks all.

-Markus
